title: Pilot acceptance, legal route mapping and egress matrix review
summary: Redwood and Orchid review pilot acceptance criteria, MSA/DPA timelines, SLA targets and an egress/cost matrix. Customer needs clarity on KMS options, SSO, and an explicit legal route for redlines; Redwood AE/SE commit to send POC pricing workbook, security pack, and a proposed redline-friendly MSA excerpt. Next steps include a legal-only readout and a bench test for 95th latency under a sample load.
topics: MSA/DPA redline process and legal owner mapping
Egress fee matrix and cost modeling
action_items: Jordan Keane | Send POC pricing workbook with reserved vs hosted scenarios | 2025-05-16
Priya Nair | Share security pack: SOC2/ISO attestation copy + DPA sample | 2025-05-15
Marcus Liu | Run 95th-latency bench with Orchid sample workload and share raw traces | 2025-05-20
Nina Patel | Provide list of mandatory DPA redlines and legal contacts for review | 2025-05-16
next_steps: Redwood to circulate a redline-friendly MSA excerpt and a DPA change log
Schedule legal-only 30min readout (requested by Orchid) for next week
Run a bench test with Orchid's sample traffic and report p50/p95/p99 numbers
Share pricing workbook and proposed pilot SOW with cost for egress scenarios
questions: What specific acceptance tests will trigger pilot completion/release to prod?
Does Orchid require customer-managed KMS (HSM) or is customer-managed keys in cloud OK?
Are there minimum committed capacity requirements for Dedicated during pilot?
How will egress charges be calculated if traffic bursts exceed estimate?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-13 14:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Recording ID: ff-20250513-orchid-0007
Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Marcus (Redwood); Sofia, Ethan, Nina, Dan (Orchid)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we're on the dot. Jordan Keane from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. Priya and Marcus are with me, Priya will cover security stuff and Marcus will run through the bench plan.
[00:18] Sofia: Thanks Jordan, Sofia here. We only have 54 minutes so want to cover legal pathing first then pilot acceptance and finally costs — egress especially.
[00:29] Jordan: Sounds good. Quick agenda: define acceptance criteria for the pilot, map MSA/DPA redlines and owners, confirm SLA targets and KMS approach, and walk the egress matrix that Ethan sent earlier.
[00:43] Ethan: Yep that's the doc, it's a bit rough but captures our worry about surprise egress fees if we pivot traffic to different regions.
[00:51] Priya: Cool i'll jump straight to security — Redwood has SOC2 Type II and we do ISO-27001, we can provision SSO via SAML or OIDC, and we have a few KMS options. For private key custody we support customer-managed keys via KMS integration and an HSM path when the customer wants air-gapped keying.
[01:15] Nina: Quick, quick question — is there an on-prem bundle for the private deployment or is that only VPC? Our legal team tends to say on-prem or nothing.
[01:26] Marcus: There's an on-prem package, though the private package is more typical, we call it Redwood Private but sometimes the export in the doc shows "Redwood Privatee" — ignore the typo — it supports both VPC-hosted and on-prem installs with optional airgap.
[01:42] Dan: Performance implications? If we go on-prem we need the same latency SLOs otherwise SRE will not approve.
[01:50] Marcus: Right, on-prem changes network characteristics but the runtime is the same; we tend to co-design the capacity profile. For the pilot we're proposing a Dedicated reserved pool to make numbers repeatable.
[02:05] Sofia: Let's land on acceptance. From our side acceptance is twofold: functional correctness with our prompt sets and nonfunctional SLOs — p95 latency under X ms for 99% of sample traffic and max error rate less than 0.5%.
[02:21] Jordan: Can you give us an X number for p95?
[02:24] Sofia: For user-facing chat flows we need p95 < 350ms on average; for batch scoring we're fine with p95 < 800ms.
[02:33] Marcus: Okay we can target that in bench. We'll validate p50/p95/p99 and provide traces. Note bench will use our quantized model variant that matches production.
[02:45] Ethan: And if bench fails, what is the rollback plan? We can't go to prod with failed numbers.
[02:50] Priya: Typical rollback is we fall back to a lower-capacity model or route to hosted fallback; there are fallback policies we can codify in the SOW.
[03:01] Nina: Legal: MSA redlines — we have a list, around indemnity, data residency obligations and the egress billing cap. Do you accept a limited liability carveout for privacy incidents?
[03:15] Jordan: We usually work with a standard carveout — let's have Redwood share a redline-ready MSA excerpt and DPA. We'll also flag sections that Orchid typically requests as non-starters.
[03:29] Nina: Okay we'll send our mandatory redlines after this call. Expect stuff in the DPA about deleted data retention windows and audit logs.
[03:37] Jordan: Noted. We'll also include KMS integration notes so legal can see technical controls to satisfy key custody asks.
[03:45] Marcus: On the KMS point — customer-managed keys via cloud KMS are common and supported. For HSM we do a managed HSM connector note, but that has additional engineering time. We'll include estimates in the workbook.
[03:59] Sofia: Timeboxed ask — we want acceptance within a six-week pilot; pilot start would be after SOW and MSA signed.
[04:09] Jordan: Six weeks ok. We'll draft SOW that is 6 weeks with milestone gating (week 2 initial integration, week 4 bench readout, week 6 acceptance).
[04:20] Ethan: Egress — our finance team insists on a matrix: region egress, per-GB fee, daily burst allowance, and a hard cap. Can Redwood provide a billing scenario table?
[04:33] Jordan: Yes we'll provide a pricing workbook with reserved vs hosted lines and an egress sensitivity table. We'll model two burst profiles.
[04:41] Nina: Also require an egress audit trail in the platform. Can we see token-level billing?
[04:49] Priya: Console supports token-level breakdowns and route-level cost. We'll add a screenshot to the security pack.
[04:57] Dan: Question on SLAs — 99.9 uptime is ok, but what about latency SLAs and credits?
[05:04] Marcus: We can commit to availability SLA for Dedicated pools; latency SLAs are softer, we typically commit to operational targets and provide credits for systemic failures, but not for per-request latency spikes caused by customer workload changes unless it's on us.
[05:20] Jordan: We'll propose language that maps pilot acceptance p95 to release criteria; legal can decide if that should flow into credits.
[05:28] Sofia: Fine. For the pilot we just need clear pass/fail criteria. If pass, we move toward a Reserved capacity contract.
[05:35] Ethan: On pricing we might need a soft commit for Reserved capacity if pilot shows steady load; what's the min term?
[05:43] Jordan: For Dedicated reserved we commonly do 3 or 12 month commits; we can propose a 3-month pilot-to-reserve conversion with pro-rated billing.
[05:53] Nina: Regarding DPA, our internal counsel often pushes additional subprocessor clauses and an audit clause. Do you permit annual audits?
[06:02] Priya: We can provide audit reports (SOC2) and a settable subprocessor list. Direct annual audit by customer teams is difficult in hosted mode, but we can arrange third-party attestation or an audit window for Private/on-prem. We'll document options.
[06:20] Marcus: Technical deep-dive — the bench plan will run your sample traffic with a 20% chaos injection to simulate spikes; we'll measure p50/p95/p99, throughput, and memory/KV cache hit rates.
[06:35] Dan: The chaos injection is good — we need to see how the KV cache behaves under prefix reuse.
[06:44] Marcus: We'll send raw traces and pre-aggregated dashboards.
[06:50] Jordan: Quick check — competitors mentioned? You're evaluating OtherCloudAI and an open-source managed vendor?
[06:57] Sofia: OtherCloudAI for price and OpenServe (i might be mispronouncing) for self-host promises.
[07:05] Jordan: Good to know. We'll highlight quantization/throughput tradeoffs in the workbook.
[07:12] Ethan: Billing: looking for a hard cap mechanism to prevent unexpected charges during pilot.
[07:19] Jordan: We can set daily spend limits and egress thresholds and alerting; for Hosted customers we can enforce soft caps and require manual uplift. For Dedicated, caps need contract terms.
[07:34] Nina: Legal ask — we'd prefer a contract-side egress cap in the SOW for pilot scope.
[07:40] Jordan: We'll propose language for a pilot cap and an escalation path if you need overage.
[07:46] Sofia: Ok. Regarding data residency, we want EU-only for PII in the pilot. Can you pin region?
[07:55] Priya: Yes we can pin routing to EU regions and restrict model serving to specific zones. We'll document network and egress paths.
[08:04] Dan: Networking question — do you support private endpoints and egress via our NAT?
[08:09] Marcus: Yes VPC peering and private endpoints supported; egress via your NAT is doable for Private. For Hosted there are egress paths we can document.
[08:19] Jordan: Let's review next steps — we'll send the pricing workbook, security pack, MSA excerpt and a proposed SOW within 48 hours. Marcus will run bench and return in one week.
[08:32] Sofia: Prefer the legal-only readout earlier; our counsel Nina would like 30 minutes next Tuesday.
[08:39] Nina: That works, send invite. Also i will email mandatory DPA redlines after the call.
[08:46] Ethan: One more thing — can we get a sample invoice line for egress so finance can pre-approve?
[08:53] Jordan: We'll include sample invoice rows in the workbook.
[09:00] Priya: Security note — retention windows: Redwood supports configurable retention and a delete-at-rest policy, we will outline the retention options and log exports.
[09:12] Sofia: Great. Alright let's open for specific legal redline mapping.
[09:18] Nina: Clause 9 indemnity — we want limited liability to include data breach caused by your negligence; add carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
[09:29] Jordan: Our standard is liability capped by fees paid in prior 12 months and carveouts for gross negligence; we will flag whether we can increase that cap for Orchid.
[09:41] Nina: Also request the right to audit subprocessors annually — you mentioned this might be hard for Hosted. Could we get a quarterly attestation?
[09:50] Priya: Quarterly attestation by Redwood is fine, with third-party SOC2 report attached. For on-prem we can open a technical audit window.
[10:01] Dan: Back to technical — if we go Dedicated reserved, can we burst to Hosted for overflow? We need a failover to prevent service disruption.
[10:10] Marcus: Yes you can configure smart routing: primary Dedicated pool with fallback to hosted compatible model; there's a policy engine to route by latency/cost/region. We'll include config examples.
[10:24] Sofia: Excellent. Any blockers on pricing for pilot?
[10:28] Ethan: Not yet, finance will review the workbook. We want both hosted and dedicated numbers.
[10:34] Jordan: We'll do both. Also including pro-rated commit conversion options.
[10:40] Nina: Time check — we're at about 10 minutes in? (note: transcript timestamps jump)
[10:45] Jordan: We're at 10 minutes, still good. Quick callouts: (1) Redwood to send MSA excerpt and DPA, (2) Orchid to send list of mandatory redlines, (3) Redwood bench by Marcus next week.
[10:59] Marcus: I'll need a sample dataset and ramp profile — can Dan share SRE sample traces?
[11:06] Dan: Yes i'll drop an anonymized sample and ramp pattern into the shared drive after this.
[11:12] Marcus: Great. Also need a test key policy — which KMS you'll use.
[11:18] Nina: We'll propose Azure Key Vault as first option, but evaluating HSM downstream.
[11:24] Priya: Azure KV supported. For HSM we'll outline timeline.
[11:31] Jordan: Any objections to scheduling legal readout Tuesday 2025-05-20 14:00 UTC?
[11:38] Nina: Works for me.
[11:41] Sofia: Works.
[11:44] Ethan: Works.
[11:46] Jordan: Okay final recap: Redwood sends pricing workbook, security pack and MSA excerpt in 48 hours; Orchid sends DPA redlines and sample traces; Marcus runs bench and returns results in one week. Legal readout scheduled.
[11:59] Sofia: Thanks all. We'll wait for the docs and bench results.
[12:05] Jordan: Thanks folks, talk soon.

End of transcript. (note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and shorthand.)
